Binding site is a coarse coordination label (metal neighbours of the closest adsorbate atom within +0.45 Å of the shortest contact: 1→atop, 2→bridge, ≥3→hollow). For weakly physisorbed alkanes the site is indicative only; the bond distance and contact pair are the robust metrics.
Geometry coverage: all 415 systems now have images on both sides. 67 MLIP slots use the exact published base GOAD image and its archived contact distance because an Omni image is unavailable; the captions identify this variant. Coordination sites and original coordinates for these base records are not archived here. These additions provide structural context; they do not change the geometries or values associated with the energy tables. Base-image and contact provenance.

The single-point columns compare energies evaluated without further geometry relaxation; the images show relaxed structures. The combined column uses the ML and DFT values displayed in the relaxed comparison. A dash means a required input is unavailable. Kestrel single-point convention: Eads(SPE) = E(complex, NSW=0) − E(relaxed slab) − E(relaxed molecule). New entries require completed, electronically converged single-point complexes and converged relaxed references with matching functional and composition, using the existing |Eads| ≤ 5 eV review screen.
Combined column: Eads(ML) − Eads(SPE) − Eads(DFT, relaxed). It uses the displayed relaxed-comparison inputs and the full-precision SPE value; all three must be available. Published SPE energies and single-point Δ values are preserved; their original ML references remain in the download. New single-point Δ values use the displayed relaxed-comparison ML value.

Energy differences: method residual and relaxation

(ML − relaxed DFT) = (ML − SPE) + (SPE − relaxed DFT). All terms here are adsorption energies in eV. Subtracting the same-geometry residual from the total leaves (ML − relaxed DFT) − (ML − SPE) = SPE − relaxed DFT, not ML − relaxed DFT − SPE.

Interpretation: ML − SPE measures a same-geometry model discrepancy only when the ML and SPE structures and adsorption-reference conventions match. It includes ML approximation error, functional differences and reference offsets; it is not a pure functional correction. SPE − relaxed DFT is a relaxation contribution only with compatible references, potentials, numerical settings and a linked initial/final geometry. It is not a functional-independent "true error".

Current evidence is descriptive: 221 complete ML/SPE/relaxed triples across 76 exact surface/molecule pairs out of 329 displayed SPE entries. Missing inputs are omitted, never treated as zero. 84 rows with explicitly marked energy-review values are excluded from these paired statistics; the tables retain their values. All panels use the same triples within each functional. Historical and audited results are mixed; geometry identity and cross-run reference compatibility have not been established. Kestrel SPE values currently subtract relaxed molecule/slab references; the newly submitted reference SPE jobs are not included. POTCAR variants were allowed by the existing publication policy, which does not establish physical reference equivalence. The existing energy screen can bias these distributions.

One ML value is used consistently per row: the displayed relaxed-comparison ML energy. Historical SPE differences sometimes used another ML reference; those published differences remain unchanged and are not used in these plots. Displayed ML/relaxed precision limits the derived differences. Formate and formic acid remain separate.

Functional sensitivity on a common cohort

56 systems have SPE values for all four functionals; ML and relaxed energies are not required for this panel. PBE+D3: -0.241 eV mean (-0.238 median); r2SCAN: -0.046 eV mean (-0.053 median); BEEF-vdW: -0.244 eV mean (-0.246 median). Negative shifts mean stronger adsorption than PBE. Pairing removes system-composition imbalance, but does not prove identical geometry or settings. These are observed method/reference shifts, not isolated exchange-correlation effects or an accuracy ranking.

Cancellation versus reinforcement

Each point is an exact surface/molecule/functional triple. Its x + y value is the total ML−relaxed discrepancy. Opposite signs cancel; equal signs reinforce. A negative gap below −0.01 eV occurs in 0 triples: these require provenance/geometry review, not clipping. For genuinely matched calculations relaxed to a lower energy with identical references, the gap should be nonnegative.

Legacy-column warning: the retained ML − SPE − DFT (relaxed) column is literal arithmetic, not an error decomposition or a corrected physical error. It is excluded from this analysis.

Ethanol and DME remain distinct despite both having formula C2H6O; formate and formic acid, and propanol and isopropanol, also remain distinct.

A blank binding energy can still have a converged complex. Binding energies require compatible complex, clean-slab and gas-molecule results. Ag111–DME PBE has completed relaxed and SPE complexes; its original gas reference failed and its standard Perlmutter slab has the wrong atom count. Converged recovery references are applied when available. Size-specific Kestrel slabs are used only when their PAW potential identities also match the complex. The potential audit supersedes the earlier variant-permissive policy.
